newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat strong on good Australia crop news.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat strong on good Australia crop news.

text.p: Australian wheat futures showed strength on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Tuesday, in contrast with Chicago's slide on Monday and despite a lack of trades.

Brokers said that good export contracts, the acknowledgement of a record 23 million tonne wheat crop by the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), a A$3.00 a tonne pool price increase offshore and the impact the Australian crop was having on sliding prices in Chicago all underpinned a strong local futures market.

Settlement prices (the mid-point between buyer and seller quotes) for the nearest-term contract March 1997 rose by A$2.50 to A$166.00 a tonne, while May 1977 gained A$6.00 and September 1997 rose by A$10.00.
Settlement gains tapered off in the more distant contracts.
"What we're seeing here today is a relatively positive tone despite the fact that Chicago was a little weaker," said Gary Booth, of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd.
"Australia particularly has had some reasonable success in sales, and it's acknowledged by many that Australia's good quality wheat will help it winning more tenders," he said.
The Australian dollar's weakness and the rising U.S. dollar added to Australian wheat's competitive edge, he said.
Record sales on the AWB's books for this time of year, as well as record shipments through New South Wales ports, showed "everything's running at full speed and running well," he said.
"The market reflects the fact that there is some buoyancy and that we hope to see more sales announced. It's a good feeling," Booth said.
The January 1997 contract left the SFE boards on Tuesday with the large number of 422 contracts delivered on, excluding Tuesday's figures.
